instruction: Lift the red can with white top and the hand-sized can with metallic finish, drop both into the hard plastic rectangular box.
system_prompt:
Use the images and state to complete the task. Reply with the next steps to execute.

ROBOT: two robot arms (left, right). Degrees of freedom per arm: 6. Maximum gripper opening: about 9 cm. End effectors — left: parallel-jaw gripper; right: parallel-jaw gripper.

COORDINATE FRAME: Positions and moves use the task axes: +x forward away from the robot body, +y to the robot's own left, +z up, not image left/right. These axes stay fixed as the camera or gripper moves. Distances are in centimetres; angles are in degrees.

WORKSPACE: Table bounds: x from 30 to 100 cm, y from -60 to 60 cm. Arm reach limits are unknown.

IMAGES (attached every turn, in this order):
- overview: workspace camera.
- left_camera: camera on the left wrist or hand.
- right_camera: camera on the right wrist or hand.
Drawn on them:
- in overview, cyan guides belong to the left arm and orange to the right. L/R circles mark each grasp point. Dashed x/y lines cross at each grasp point's height; the z line runs downward. Ticks are 5 cm apart, with coordinate labels every 10 cm. Compare positions at the same height: objects above or below the guides appear shifted by perspective;
- the corner legend shows the image directions of +x, +y and +z; an end-on axis is a dot;
- follow short leader lines from offset labels to their ticks; not every tick is labelled.
No coordinate guides are drawn in: left_camera, right_camera.

GRIPPER: Positions refer to the grasp points: midway between the fingers, 3.5 cm short of their ends. 'approach' is a unit vector pointing along the fingers; 'finger axis' is a unit vector along their opening/closing direction. Both use the task axes.
Opening ranges from 0 (closed) to 1 (open). 'Measured opening' is sensor feedback; 'commanded opening' is the requested setting. Use the images to check the grasp, not opening alone.

ACTIONS: "steps" is an ordered list. Each step has a command list for each arm:
{"left": [...], "right": [...]}. The two arms act simultaneously.
Each arm's list defines one combined motion:
- rotate, point and home set the pose first, in the order written.
- Moves then add up along each axis from that pose. For example, ["move z +5", "move z -14"] gives one move of -9 cm, not two separate moves.
- The motion planner chooses the path to the target; it may not be straight.
- The gripper opens or closes during the motion. To close after arriving, put "gripper close" in the next step.
Use ["wait"] for an inactive arm.

Commands (one string each; omit the arm name):
  move x|y|z <cm>              move along a task axis without changing orientation.
  rotate roll|pitch|yaw <deg>  rotate about task x|y|z respectively, through its reference point.
  point down|forward|down45   point the fingers down (-z), forward (+x), or halfway between; set the finger axis to +y.
  gripper open|close|<0..1>   set the opening: 0 is closed, 1 is open.
  home                       return to the arm's initial position and orientation.
  wait                       take no action.
Example: [{"left": ["move x +5"], "right": ["move x +5"]},
          {"left": ["gripper close"], "right": ["gripper close"]}]
To request a stop, include the string "done" in "steps".

CONVERSATION: earlier messages, when present, show the previous turn (without images). Use it to track changes and past attempts. Choose the next actions from the current observation.

RESPONSE FORMAT: reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{
  "progress": "<the current subtask, without a prefix>",
  "steps": [{"left": ["<command>", ...], "right": ["<command>", ...]}, ...]
}
If a step is FAILED or INVALID, the remaining steps in this turn are SKIPPED. Check the next observation before continuing.
Use "done" to request a stop when no further action is needed. It does not confirm success. If another observation follows, reassess the task before continuing.
